frequency_question: How often do central banks with active CCyB frameworks increase the buffer above 0% during periods of perceived economic expansion within a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Members are established jurisdictions with an operational CCyB framework (e.g., Bank of England FPC, Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Federal Reserve Board of Governors) evaluated over distinct macroprudential guidance windows. Excluded are jurisdictions without an active framework or where the buffer was already active and being adjusted sequentially.

coverage_note: 7 named instances across major jurisdictions and Federal Reserve multi-year checkpoints.
known_gaps: Does not account for idiosyncratic US regulatory preferences relative to European peers.
skeleton: Global peer central bank standard activation frequency applied to the Federal Reserve institutional posture.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 7 observations across comparable peer/temporal windows
validity_reason: Macroprudential frameworks and institutional mindsets on capital buffers evolve slowly over multi-year structural horizons.
